## What you need

- **Must (headline):** ML fundamentals, Python (production), PyTorch, Research methods & re-implementation.
- **Important (headline):** Safety & capability evals, Alignment methods, Interpretability, Red-teaming, Novel research & publications.
- **Full inventory:** 41 skills (Must 4 · Important 13 · Should 20 · Optional 4), each with its evidence and posting keywords: [ai-safety-researcher.md](../../03-skills-and-tech/inventories/ai-safety-researcher.md).
- **Prerequisites:** PhD or a fellowship is typical; ~600 technical FTEs worldwide (single-author estimate, C)
- What to learn first and what to drop across roles: [skills radar](../../03-skills-and-tech/skills-radar.md); in what order: [learning roadmaps](../../03-skills-and-tech/learning-roadmaps.md).

## How to prove it

- **What the evidence asks for:** Fellowship projects; published safety research; open eval contributions
- **Project archetypes that cover the most of its Must and Important skills** (Grade M): [P18 Safety / interpretability research project](../../05-portfolio/project-archetypes.md#p18) (77%); [P8 Paper re-implementation with rigorous evals and a write-up](../../05-portfolio/project-archetypes.md#p8) (55%); [P4 Prompt vs RAG vs fine-tune comparison](../../05-portfolio/project-archetypes.md#p4) (41%). One project rarely covers a role; [job-search strategy §2.6](../../06-job-search/job-search-strategy.md#26-the-constraints-that-bind-first) computes the smallest sets that do.
- How verifiable the proof must be, and what to publish: [proof-of-work standards](../../05-portfolio/proof-of-work-standards.md).
